cards.card: 三菱ＵＦＪカード ゴールド
三菱ＵＦＪカード・プラチナ・アメリカン・エキスプレス・カード
JCB カード W plus L

note: Japan's three largest banking groups issue their credit cards through their card companies: MUFG through Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS, SMBC through Sumitomo Mitsui Card, and Mizuho through its card partners. Sumitomo Mitsui Card's and Mizuho Bank's sites refuse this research's requests (Akamai, 'Access Denied', 2026-10-30), so JCB, the country's own card brand and one of its largest issuers, is written in their place. Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS's pages, as of 28 September 2026, read 2026-10-30: the MUFG Card (三菱ＵＦＪカード) has no annual fee, ever; the MUFG Card Gold costs 11,000 yen a year including tax, its first-year waiver being for those who join on the web, a condition the game doesn't check, so the fee is written in full; the MUFG Card Platinum American Express costs 22,000 yen a year. Revolving (its registered revolving service, 楽Ｐａｙ) carries 19.80% a year (実質年率, charged by the day on the balance carried, written as a yearly rate), which replaces the 18.00% this file held from 2026-10-29; the page says a few cards differ, without naming them, and 19.80% is written on all three. A cash advance (キャッシングサービス) carries 17.95% a year (融資利率, 実質年率). The annual-fee reduction for revolving users, the ETC and UnionPay cards' issue fees, the statement-by-post fee and the late charge (遅延損害金, set in the member agreement as the statutory rate, read but not written, the game having no statutory rate) aren't written; nor is a foreign-transaction fee, the member agreement (個人会員規約, read 2026-10-30) adding only 'a fee the company sets' to the exchange rate without a figure. JCB's pages (as of August 2026, read 2026-10-30): the JCB Card W and W plus L (open to those 18 to 39 when they apply, an age the game doesn't check at application) and the JCB Card S have no annual fee; JCB Gold costs 11,000 yen a year including tax, its first year free; JCB Platinum 27,500 yen. Revolving carries 18.00% a year (実質年率), to which JCB moved its cards from 1 October 2026 (some cards may differ, the page says). JCB's cash advance rate, minimum payment and foreign-transaction fee weren't found on the pages read and aren't written. Japanese cards are paid in full each month by default (monthly closing on the 15th, payment on the 10th of the next month), revolving only where the holder chooses it; no grace period in the game's sense is stated.
